title: feat(cli): serve the Console document with a nonce-based content-security-policy
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoBVXzK6k7CamM6jB1PW7zzb)_

## Summary

The Console document (every HTML answer under `/_console/`) is now served with a nonce-based `content-security-policy` response header. Until now only API responses carried a policy (`packages/runtime/src/security/security-headers.ts`), and the Console shell carried none.

- `createConsoleStaticPlugin` (`packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts`) draws a fresh 128-bit nonce per response. It names the nonce in the header and stamps it on every script element of the served document: the build's inline scripts, its module entry, and the server's own react-pages disable script.
- The nonce is stamped before any request-time value (branding title and meta tags) is written into the document, so no runtime value can carry it.
- This plugin is the one place the document is served from. `os dev` and `os start` both spawn `os serve`, which mounts it, and the Docker image's command is `os start`. A host that mounts the plugin itself through `@objectstack/cli/console` gets the same header.
- Runtime is unchanged.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## The policy

Each allowance was measured against the published `@objectstack/console@18.0.0` build (its `index.html`, its `assets/`) and the objectui source at the pinned `.objectui-sha` (`2958f17e`). The reason for each is written next to the policy in the code.

| Directive | Value | Why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `default-src` | `'self'` | Covers maplibre's module workers (started from its own file), the PWA manifest and same-origin frames (the Studio live canvas). The build ships no web fonts. |
| `script-src` | `'self' 'nonce-…' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, plus `'unsafe-eval'` only while the react-pages tier is on | `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` is for shiki (the AI chat's code highlighter), which compiles WebAssembly. The `kind:'react'` runtime (ADR-0081) evaluates page source with `Function`, so `'unsafe-eval'` follows `OS_PAGE_REACT`. That flag is read once per document, so the disable script and the policy always agree. |
| `style-src` | `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` | The shell's boot-splash style element, React/Radix `style` attributes, and style elements libraries insert at run time without a nonce. |
| `img-src` | `'self' data: blob: https:` | Inline SVG icons in the stylesheets, upload previews, and externally hosted branding logos and favicons, avatars, image field values and email-template images. |
| `connect-src` | `'self' https://demotiles.maplibre.org`, plus the error-reporting DSN's origin when the runtime serves one, plus `OS_CONSOLE_CSP_CONNECT_SRC` | The API (`'self'` also covers the same-origin WebSocket and event stream), and the map view's default style host. The DSN origin is read from the same `GET /api/v1/runtime/config` answer the document's branding is already read from. |
| `object-src` | `'none'` | |
| `base-uri` | `'self'` | Only the server's own base element. |
| `frame-ancestors` | `'self'`, omitted on `/_console/f/*` | The public-forms screen gives authors an iframe snippet that embeds the public form page on their own site. |

### What an operator may notice

- **New `OS_CONSOLE_CSP_CONNECT_SRC`.** It is a space-separated list of extra `connect-src` sources: a scheme (`https:`) or a scheme with a host (`https://tiles.example.com`). It exists because a map view's authored `mapStyle` is fetched straight from its host, and the server cannot know that host ahead of the request. It is read once at boot. An entry outside that grammar (a keyword, `*`, a bare host, or anything carrying `;` or quotes) stops the boot with a message naming it.
- **Framing from another origin is refused**, except on the public form page.
- **The Studio's code editor** (Monaco) loads its core from a public CDN. The policy deliberately lists no CDN in `script-src`, because a CDN host there admits every file that CDN serves. The editor therefore shows the plain-text fallback objectui already ships for this case.

## Verification

Tests: a new suite, `packages/cli/src/utils/console.content-security-policy.test.ts`, with 17 cases. It boots the real plugin on a real Hono app, and adds the real `RuntimeConfigPlugin` for the DSN case. It checks:

- the header is present on the shell, on an SPA fallback and on a direct `.html` hit, and absent on assets;
- the nonce differs across 5 responses;
- every script element in the served document carries the header's nonce, including an uppercase tag and the injected react-pages disable script;
- `'unsafe-eval'` is present by default and absent with `OS_PAGE_REACT=off`;
- `frame-ancestors` is omitted on `/_console/f/*` and kept on `/_console/forms/*`;
- the DSN origin appears without its key;
- `OS_CONSOLE_CSP_CONNECT_SRC` extras are added in order, and five malformed values refuse the boot.

Local results, at head `9182f4b9`:

- The full `@objectstack/cli` unit tier (`vitest run --project unit`) passes: 328 files, 4829 tests. The integration tier is left to CI, because the diff touches no spawn entry.
- `vitest run --project unit` passes on the new suite plus `console.branded-head`, `console.public-form-redirect`, `console.asset-cache`, `console.not-built`, `console.sha-drift`, `published-subpath-console.pin` and `runtime-assets`. The existing suites pass unchanged.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (tsc plus `check:test-typecheck`) exits 0. `eslint --no-inline-config` on both touched files exits 0.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 69 commands, and all 69 exit 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reports 69 derived, 69 run, 0 not measured.

Browser smoke: `pnpm dev -- --fresh -p <port>` (the showcase), serving the published `@objectstack/console@18.0.0` dist, driven by Playwright Chromium.

- The run signed in as the seeded admin and visited eight routes: home, the showcase app, a `kind:'react'` page (Task Desk), a map page, the component gallery, the capability map, `/ai`, and a public form URL.
- A `securitypolicyviolation` listener was installed before any page script ran, and console messages were captured too.
- A negative control at the end of each run proved the listener can see a refusal. It inserts an inline script without a nonce, and a script from the Monaco CDN path. Both were refused and both were reported.

| Run | Header on the wire | Violations on the 8 routes | Page errors |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| react pages **on** (default) | `'unsafe-eval'` present | **0** | 0 |
| `OS_PAGE_REACT=off` | `'unsafe-eval'` absent | 1 per document load, all the same one (see Acceptance notes) | 0 |

In both runs the map rendered its canvas. The Task Desk react page rendered with the tier on, and showed the disabled notice with it off. `frame-ancestors` was absent only on the public form URL.

## Acceptance notes

- **With `OS_PAGE_REACT=off`, each document load reports one `script-src` `eval` refusal from the Console bundle.** The source is zod v4's capability probe: it tries `Function('')` once inside a try/catch, to decide whether its JIT can be used, and falls back when refused. Nothing breaks, and the page reports no error. The probe is skipped when zod's `jitless` config is set, so the clean fix is objectui-side: set `z.config({ jitless: true })` in the Console, at least when react pages are off. That is outside this repository and is reported to the maintainer rather than worked around here, for example by allowing `'unsafe-eval'`.
- **Monaco.** The code editor's CDN load is refused by design, as above. Self-hosting Monaco in objectui would restore the full editor under this policy.
- **Out of scope.** Where the Console keeps its session token is a separate decision, and this PR does not change it.
